title: Clay Pot Rice and Short Ribs

items: 3 shallots or ¼ red onion, chopped (½” segments)
1 red sweet pepper (½” segments, mediterranean or bell)
4 green onions, sliced (reserve the green slices for garnish)
2 fresno chili peppers, sliced or minced
¼ cup douchi (chinese fermented black beans)
6 baby bok choi (or choice of hearty but leafy greens)
Thinly sliced spring onions or scallions, green parts only, for serving

steps: Wash the rice then cover with water and soak for 30 minutes.  Drain when done.
Soak the shitake mushrooms for 15 minutes, then mince when done.
Slice the shortribs into bitesize pieces then add to a bowl with water and tenderizer/baking soda and soak for 15 minutes.  Rinse and squeeze out excess water when done.
Place a clay pot (or cast iron dutch oven) on the stove and preheat over low heat.
Roughly chop the shallots and sweet pepper and set aside.
Finely chop the garlic, ginger, green onions (whites), douchi and place in a large bowl.
Add the shortrib, oyster sauce, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, and white pepper and mix to evenly coat.
Add the Shallots and sweet pepper then mix briefly to distribute.
Increase the stove heat to medium and brush a generous amount of oil inside the pot to coat the bottom and sides.
Add the soaked rice and distribute so that it sits level.  The rice should sizzle when you add it.
Add enough water to barely cover the rice, approximately 3-4 cups, then cover and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the meat mixture on top of the rice and drizzle 1-2 Tbsp of oil along the sides of the pot.  Cover and cook an additional 10 minutes over medium to medium-low heat.
Layer bok choi leaves over the cooked meat then cover and cook for 3 more minutes.
The clay pot rice dish is done when the meat is cooked through and tender, the greens are lightly steamed, and a crispy golden brown crust of rice formed along the bottom of the pot.
Serve with a garnish of sliced green onions, cilantro, sesame seeds, a crispy fried egg, and a splash of mild soy sauce.
reviewFlags: The source does not say when to add the soaked shiitake mushrooms. Some serving garnishes have no listed quantities.
